title: Quick start
description: Run an office, mint a token, and message your first agent from the terminal.

sections.title: Start the office
paragraphs: Clone the repository and start the server. The Flox environment pins Bun, Node, and the native build toolchain; without Flox, install Bun 1.4.2 and Node 24 yourself and run bun install.
sections.code:
git clone https://github.com/smeltery/bureau.git
cd bureau
flox activate     # or: bun install
bun run dev

sections.title: Claim the office
paragraphs: Open http://localhost:4000 on the server machine. The first visit asks for your name and makes you the owner; claiming only works from the machine itself. Click an empty desk to spawn your first agent and sign in to its provider when asked.

sections.title: Create an API token
paragraphs: Open User Settings → API tokens, give the token a name such as "laptop scripts", and choose an expiry of 30 days, a year, or never. Copy it now: Bureau stores only a hash and shows the token once.

sections.title: Send your first message
paragraphs: List your agents, pick an id, and send it a message. The call returns as soon as the message is accepted; the agent works on it in the office like any other message.
sections.code:
curl -s "$BUREAU_URL/api/agents" -H "Authorization: Bearer $BUREAU_TOKEN" | jq -r '.[] | "\(.id)  \(.name)"'

curl -s -X POST "$BUREAU_URL/api/agents/$AGENT_ID/messages" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BUREAU_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"text":"Summarize the open TODOs in this repo"}'

sections.title: Read the reply
paragraphs: Drain your token’s inbox to read what the agent sent back. Entries with direction from_agent are replies; to_agent entries echo what you sent. Pass the latestSequence from one drain as after on the next to get only new entries.

sections.title: If the first request fails
paragraphs: Check GET /readyz first; it needs no token and separates connectivity problems from authentication problems. A 401 means the token is missing, mistyped, revoked, or expired. A 403 means the agent is in a room your account cannot see.
A 409 on send means the agent is not accepting messages right now, for example while it is stopped. A 429 means its queue already holds 50 messages; wait for it to catch up.
